harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) as a NAT gateway for a new private network (10.10.20.0/24) shared with node2 and node3, using an Ansible playbook run from the control node (node4). node1's eth1 got address 10.10.20.1/24 plus a masquerade source-NAT rule out eth0; node2/node3 got static addresses (10.10.20.2/3) on enp8s0 via netplan and a preferred default route via node1. Verified processes on node2/node3 reach the internet (curl 1.1.1.1 -> HTTP 301) exclusively through node1's NAT (ip route get shows the private gateway as the path, and node1's nftables/conntrack show translated hits). All four nodes were then restarted one at a time via systemctl reboot, with boot_id changes proving real restarts and post-restart re-verification (NAT rule/interface persisted via VyOS saved config, netplan persisted on Ubuntu, Ansible re-run idempotent with continued internet reachability) confirming full recovery.
actions_performed: Surveyed topology: node1=VyOS router with eth0 (mgmt/egress) + eth1 (unconfigured private NIC), node2/node3=Ubuntu 24.04 with enp1s0 (mgmt) + enp8s0 (unconfigured private NIC), node4=Ansible control node.

Bootstrapped SSH access: enabled ssh.service on node2/node3 (generated host keys, fixed missing /run/sshd), installed cluster SSH pubkey as authorized_keys on node1/node2/node3, created a dedicated VyOS 'ansible' admin user (public-key auth, sudo/vyattacfg groups, NOPASSWD sudo) since VyOS disables root SSH login by default.

Diagnosed a VyOS cli-shell-api session-setup bug that silently no-ops 'configure'/'set' when invoked as a non-root user without an escalated session; fixed by having the Ansible play 'become: root' via sudo for VyOS configuration tasks.

Wrote an Ansible project on node4 (~/nat-egress/inventory.ini, playbook.yml): play 1 configures node1's eth1 IP and NAT masquerade source rule via VyOS configure/commit/save; play 2 writes netplan static IP + preferred default route via node1 on node2/node3, applies it, and verifies internet reachability.
Ran the playbook successfully; verified via ip route get, nftables counters, and conntrack that node2/node3 internet traffic is NATed through node1.

Executed the mandatory restart-evidence protocol: captured boot_id + health baseline on all 4 nodes, restarted each one at a time (node1, node2, node3, node4) via systemctl reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed boot_id changed on each, and verified NAT/routing/Ansible functionality fully recovered after each restart, including a final full playbook re-run confirming idempotent, healthy end state.

evidence.requirement: Baseline topology/network survey (node1 VyOS w/ eth0+eth1, node2/node3 Ubuntu w/ enp1s0+enp8s0, node4 ansible control node)
evidence.summary: Confirmed node1 has eth0 (mgmt) + eth1 (unconfigured private NIC), node2/node3 have enp1s0 (mgmt) + enp8s0 (unconfigured private NIC), node4 is the ansible control node.

evidence.requirement: SSH access bootstrap for Ansible (host keys, authorized_keys, VyOS ansible user)
evidence.summary: ssh enabled on node2/node3, cluster pubkey authorized on node1/node2/node3, VyOS 'ansible' admin user created and confirmed to log in with sudo working.

evidence.requirement: Ansible playbook configures NAT + private network addressing (task's core requirement)
evidence.summary: Playbook syntax-checked and executed cleanly from node4 against inventory of node1 (router) and node2/node3 (private_clients): applied VyOS eth1 IP + NAT masquerade rule, and netplan static IPs + preferred default route via node1 on the clients.

evidence.requirement: Verification that node2/node3 reach the internet only through node1's NAT
evidence.summary: Baseline showed node2's default route bypassing node1; after playbook run, ip route get 1.1.1.1 on node2/node3 shows path via 10.10.20.1 dev enp8s0, curl returns HTTP 301, and node1's nftables counters + conntrack show live translated flows from 10.10.20.2/.3.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered NAT/interface state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 2674ee60...; reboot acked; post-restart boot_id 5e8d2639... (changed, uptime 23s); eth1 IP, NAT nftables rule, and ip_forward all confirmed intact after reboot.

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered private-network route/internet access
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 3fad4432...; reboot acked; post-restart boot_id b3c291ea... (changed, uptime 4s); enp8s0 static IP, default route via node1, and curl HTTP 301 all confirmed recovered.

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered private-network route/internet access
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 92ec88af...; reboot acked; post-restart boot_id 557e763d... (changed, uptime 4s); enp8s0 static IP, default route via node1, and curl HTTP 301 all confirmed recovered.

evidence.requirement: node4 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered Ansible control-node functionality and overall system health
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id adba3716...; reboot acked; post-restart boot_id 6c46deb9... (changed, uptime 5s); nat-egress project files intact, ansible functional, and a full idempotent playbook re-run confirmed node2/node3 still reach the internet (HTTP 301) through node1's NAT.
